authenticated.intent: Tenant access is evaluated against a non-null auth identity and the final organization relationship for the row.

anon.intent: No tenant or operator data access; only deliberately public catalog and published ontology reads may be reachable.

requiredCompensatingControls: Authenticate the caller before creating the privileged client.
Filter privileged child reads and writes by organization and site in addition to parent identifiers.
Enforce same-tenant relationships with database integrity controls where approved.
Never expose live credentials or raw bearer tokens in artifacts or telemetry.

boundaryCatalog.name: organizations
boundaryCatalog.observed: owner_id is the RLS ownership anchor; it is nullable and has no migration foreign key to the auth identity store.
boundaryCatalog.proposedInvariant: An authenticated actor can reach an organization row only when the final row owner is that actor; owner transfer is not a generic update.

boundaryCatalog.name: sites
boundaryCatalog.observed: Tenant policy ownership is derived through organization_id, while related site_id values are not consistently proven to belong to the same organization.
boundaryCatalog.proposedInvariant: Every non-null site reference resolves to a site in the row organization before a row is returned or accepted.

boundaryCatalog.name: workpack and children
boundaryCatalog.observed: Several service-role child queries validate an owned workpack and then filter children only by workpack_id.
boundaryCatalog.proposedInvariant: A privileged child query includes the owned organization_id and site_id when applicable, and every supplied related identifier is re-owned before use.

boundaryCatalog.name: legacy documents
boundaryCatalog.observed: The table contains body and citation fields, has no RLS declaration in migrations, and has no documented public or operator classification.
boundaryCatalog.proposedInvariant: Direct anon and authenticated access remains denied until a separate owner explicitly classifies and scopes this legacy table.

boundaryCatalog.name: query logs
boundaryCatalog.observed: The table can contain sensitive query text and has no RLS declaration in migrations.
boundaryCatalog.proposedInvariant: Only an approved operator path may write or read query logs; anon and authenticated roles have no direct row access.

boundaryCatalog.name: dispatch
boundaryCatalog.observed: The row policy accepts a null organization branch, and the authenticated service-role route accepts an external workpackId without re-owning it.
boundaryCatalog.proposedInvariant: Tenant dispatch rows always have an owned organization and any site/workpack relation resolves inside that organization; global operator events use a separate boundary.

boundaryCatalog.name: MCP token and memory
boundaryCatalog.observed: A database token row becomes authContext siteId/orgId; memory reads filter by siteId without independently comparing orgId.
boundaryCatalog.proposedInvariant: A token has one valid scope combination, its site belongs to its organization, and every MCP memory read applies both site and organization scope.

boundaryCatalog.name: managed storage objects
boundaryCatalog.observed: The bucket is declared private and the service-role route generates organization-prefixed paths, but live object policies, grants, ownership, and direct-client reachability were not inspected.
boundaryCatalog.proposedInvariant: An object path, metadata row, organization, workpack, and improvement all agree before upload, read, overwrite, move, or delete; foreign prefixes do not reveal object existence.

boundaryCatalog.name: public catalog and ontology
boundaryCatalog.observed: Public reads are broader than the intended published content at the ingestion-run and ontology-edge boundaries.
boundaryCatalog.proposedInvariant: Anon sees only deliberate catalog fields and fully published, cited ontology subgraphs; operator metadata and embeddings remain server-only.

findings.title: Two legacy exposed-schema tables have no RLS declaration
exploitPrerequisites: The caller role has the corresponding object command privilege.
The target relation is reachable through the selected API surface.
Sensitive or attacker-influenced rows exist for the attempted command.
falsePositiveCaveats: A row policy is evaluated only after object privilege makes the command reachable.
The preserved HEAD observation saw anon SELECT reachability and zero rows, not row-body exposure.
Mutation privileges and the effective grant source were not inspected.

findings.title: `dispatch_logs` has a role-agnostic global-null CRUD branch
exploitPrerequisites: The caller role has the object privilege for the attempted command, or reaches a service-role route that performs it.
A null-organization row is present or can be accepted.
For cross-linked records, the caller knows a usable related identifier.
falsePositiveCaveats: The audit observed six service-role rows and zero anon-visible rows but did not inspect whether any row had a null organization.
Mutation privileges were not tested.
The policy branch alone does not grant a command privilege.

findings.title: Tenant policies do not enforce same-organization relationships and service-role child queries trust them
exploitPrerequisites: A foreign valid UUID is known or otherwise supplied.
A row with the caller-owned organization and a foreign related identifier is accepted or already exists.
A direct-table attempt has the corresponding object privilege, or the authenticated dispatch route uses service role on the caller's behalf.
A privileged child query includes the mismatched row in its response or downstream operation.
falsePositiveCaveats: Foreign UUID knowledge was not proven.
No mismatched row was created and no cross-tenant response injection was reproduced.
The dispatch route does not require client database INSERT privilege, but it still requires a usable foreign workpack identifier.
Some routes already validate an owned parent; the gap is the missing same-tenant relationship or child filter.

findings.title: History-like tenant tables receive unrestricted owner UPDATE and DELETE
exploitPrerequisites: The authenticated role has UPDATE or DELETE object privilege.
The target row satisfies the current owner predicate.
The command is reachable directly or through a future application path.
falsePositiveCaveats: Effective UPDATE and DELETE grants were not inspected.
The current UI may not expose those commands.
No mutation was executed.

findings.title: Ingestion-run operational metadata has an unrestricted SELECT row policy
exploitPrerequisites: Anon or authenticated has SELECT object privilege.
Operational report_path or details values are present.
The caller reaches the raw table or an unsanitized server response.
falsePositiveCaveats: The policy does not itself confer the SELECT object privilege.
HEAD observed two anon-visible rows but did not retrieve row bodies.
Effective grant catalog entries were not inspected.

findings.title: `mcp_tokens` tenant binding is not schema-enforced
exploitPrerequisites: A privileged path creates or retains an orphaned or mismatched token row.
The token carries a valid foreign siteId into MCP resolution.
The token is presented to a memory-reading tool with an allowed scope.
falsePositiveCaveats: The normal issuance API derives siteId and orgId from one owned workspace context.
No wrongly bound token was created.
No cross-tenant MCP memory read was reproduced.

findings.title: Published ontology edges do not require published endpoint nodes
exploitPrerequisites: A published edge references at least one endpoint that is not published.
The caller has SELECT object privilege.
The public path returns edge identifiers, relations, citations, or metadata.
falsePositiveCaveats: Different service-role and anon edge counts do not prove an invalid endpoint relation.
Endpoint publication consistency was not inspected.
No violating edge was identified.

findings.title: Tenant policies omit explicit roles and FORCE RLS
exploitPrerequisites: A broader role has the corresponding object privilege and falls inside an implicit policy target.
For table-owner risk, SQL executes as the table owner or another owner-equivalent path.
For the dispatch null branch, a reachable null-organization row exists or can be created.
falsePositiveCaveats: Standard owner predicates evaluate false for an unauthenticated null auth identity.
Object command privilege remains a prerequisite.
FORCE does not constrain service_role BYPASSRLS.
Live roles, owners, grants, and FORCE flags were not inspected.

findings.title: Service-only RPC intent is not reflected in grants or function hardening
exploitPrerequisites: A non-intended role has function execution privilege.
The RPC is reachable through the selected API surface.
Namespace resolution or object privileges expose a useful target.
falsePositiveCaveats: Current invoker behavior means non-bypass callers still face table RLS.
The embeddings endpoint returned 404 in the preserved probe.
Effective function execution grants were not inspected.

findings.title: Ontology publication policy does not require provenance
exploitPrerequisites: A service-role or equivalent bypass path writes a published row with empty provenance.
The public caller has SELECT object privilege.
The public graph path returns the violating row.
falsePositiveCaveats: The normal application path rejects or drops empty-provenance rows.
No direct privileged write was executed.
No current published row with empty cited_uids was proven.

approvalDecisionTable.title: Policy-only RLS and command semantics
approvalDecisionTable.smallestSafeScope: Close missing RLS intent for query_logs and documents; remove the dispatch null-tenant branch; target policies to explicit roles; split required SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE behavior with explicit new-row checks; make ingestion metadata operator-only; add ontology publication predicates without route changes.
approvalDecisionTable.approvalReason: The selected implementation would change database policies, privileges, functions, or integrity behavior and must be rehearsed as an approval-gated migration even though this packet contains no executable migration text.
approvalDecisionTable.recommendedDecision: APPROVE FOR STAGING DESIGN AND REHEARSAL ONLY; production remains separately gated.
approvalDecisionTable.rollbackUnit: One policy-only database change set with captured pre-change policy, grant, owner, and function metadata.

approvalDecisionTable.title: Tenant and service-role route scoping
approvalDecisionTable.smallestSafeScope: Route and server-library changes only: re-own supplied IDs, apply organization and site filters to privileged child queries, validate dispatch workpack ownership, and require MCP site-to-organization agreement before memory access.
approvalDecisionTable.approvalReason: A route-only implementation is not a database hard-gate action, but the current instruction authorizes an approval packet only; an explicit follow-up selection is required before code changes.
approvalDecisionTable.recommendedDecision: APPROVE AS A SEPARATE CODE BATCH after owner assignments and route acceptance cases are accepted.
approvalDecisionTable.rollbackUnit: One application deployment commit with no database or storage mutation.

approvalDecisionTable.title: FORCE RLS tradeoff decision
approvalDecisionTable.smallestSafeScope: Inventory table owners and owner-executed jobs, rehearse owner behavior in staging, and decide table by table whether FORCE is compatible; do not treat FORCE as a service-role control.
approvalDecisionTable.approvalReason: Changing FORCE state alters database authorization behavior and can break table-owner maintenance paths.
approvalDecisionTable.recommendedDecision: DEFER ENABLEMENT until the owner and maintenance-path inventory is complete; keep it out of Batch A.
approvalDecisionTable.rollbackUnit: Independent per-table FORCE state change set; ordinary RLS remains enabled during rollback.

approvalDecisionTable.title: Managed storage boundary
approvalDecisionTable.smallestSafeScope: Choose service-route-only or direct-client access, inspect staging storage policy and grant state, enforce path-to-metadata tenant agreement, and test foreign identifiers and prefixes before any production change.
approvalDecisionTable.approvalReason: Storage policy changes, bucket/object operations, and fixture uploads are database or network data mutations and require explicit approval.
approvalDecisionTable.recommendedDecision: APPROVE STAGING INSPECTION PLAN; default to service-route-only unless a direct-client requirement is demonstrated.
approvalDecisionTable.rollbackUnit: Storage policy snapshot plus application deployment; test objects are tracked by fixture IDs for staging-only cleanup.

approvalDecisionTable.title: Live cross-tenant staging tests
approvalDecisionTable.smallestSafeScope: Provision disposable organization A/B, site A/B, authenticated A/B users, tenant rows, MCP tokens, and storage objects in non-production; execute the exact pre/post matrices and remove only tagged fixtures after evidence capture.
approvalDecisionTable.approvalReason: The plan creates, updates, and deletes staging identities, rows, tokens, and objects; no production execution is authorized.
approvalDecisionTable.recommendedDecision: MANDATORY BEFORE LAUNCH PASS; execute only after approving the fixture target and cleanup manifest.
approvalDecisionTable.rollbackUnit: Tagged staging fixture set with an allowlisted cleanup manifest and post-cleanup count verification.

Logs contain a redacted authorization reason and no credential or row body.

requiredCases: Anon receives only the documented public response shape.
No organization, site, workpack, worker, token, raw ingestion details, private ontology row, or storage metadata leaks.
Authenticated tenant context does not broaden a public/global response.
Error responses do not reveal foreign resource existence.
Public behavior required by the product remains available after policy changes.

backupAndEvidenceCapture: Pin the application revision, migration history, and target project identifier without storing credentials.
Capture staging policy, role target, object privilege, default privilege, owner, function, FORCE, and storage policy metadata in an access-controlled operations record.
Take an encrypted staging backup and a schema-only authorization snapshot; record restore ownership and expiry outside this repository.
Record per-table total rows and per-organization rows for the 13 tenant tables, plus operator/public table counts.
Create a fixture manifest before mutation so cleanup is allowlisted by exact IDs and the fixture tag.
preChangeDataIntegrityChecks: Count null organization_id values in dispatch_logs and classify each as tenant or operator intent.
Count organization/site/workpack/worker/share/improvement relationship mismatches without changing rows.
Verify every mcp_tokens site/org pair is complete and consistent and no plaintext token is stored.
Count published ontology rows with empty provenance and edges with unpublished endpoints.
Compare storage metadata bucket/path prefixes with organization, workpack, and improvement ownership where staging access is approved.
Record row counts and stable identifiers required to prove no silent loss after each batch.
rehearsalSequence: Restore or refresh an isolated, sanitized staging target and verify the backup restore procedure.
Provision the tagged A/B fixture set only after Batch E approval.
Execute the pre matrix and record actual outcomes without treating a known source weakness as success.
Apply approved Batch A only; rerun policy, public-surface, data-integrity, and rollback checks.
Apply approved Batch B only; rerun all 21 service-role route cases and data-integrity checks.
Inspect and rehearse Batch D under the selected storage access model.
Evaluate Batch C separately after owner and maintenance-path inventory; never bundle it silently with Batch A.
Execute the post matrix, verify positive controls, rehearse rollback for each batch, and repeat the launch gate after rollback and reapply.
postChangeDataIntegrityChecks: All preexisting row counts and per-organization distributions match the recorded baseline except explicitly tagged fixtures.
Required payout-equivalent application fields are not relevant here; for this product, all workpack, worker, site, evidence, and storage metadata fields required by the audited routes remain present.
No new null tenant key or cross-tenant relationship mismatch is introduced.
No valid same-tenant row becomes orphaned or silently hidden from its owner.
MCP token scope pairs remain consistent and token plaintext is absent from database extracts and logs.
Public catalog and ontology outputs contain only the approved public shape.
Storage metadata and object prefixes agree for all tagged test objects.

stopSignals: Any cross-tenant operation returns or mutates a row or object.
Any denial reveals whether a foreign resource exists.
Any required same-tenant or deliberate public control fails after a batch.
Any unplanned row-count or relationship-integrity change appears.
Any credential-like value appears in an artifact or log.

A: Restore the captured policy, role target, privilege, function, and authorization metadata as one reviewed staging rollback unit.
Prefer fail-closed access during diagnosis; do not broadly reopen direct client access merely to restore availability.
Rerun the 112 symmetric negative assertions and 28 matrix positive controls after rollback.
B: Redeploy the prior application commit without changing database state.
Invalidate or rotate only credentials proven exposed; do not rotate speculatively without an operations record.
Rerun the affected route's own-tenant and foreign-tenant cases.
C: Revert only the affected table's FORCE state if an owner-executed maintenance path fails.
Keep ordinary RLS enabled and retain Batch A role/command semantics.
D: Restore the captured storage policy snapshot and prior application deployment.
Remove only fixture-tagged objects and verify metadata/object cleanup parity.
E: Delete only exact IDs in the staging fixture manifest after evidence is sealed.
Verify post-cleanup table/object counts against the pre-fixture baseline.
Do not run fixture cleanup against production.

launchGate: All 10 findings have an approved disposition and no P1 finding remains open for launch.
Batch A and Batch B staging rehearsals pass with unchanged non-fixture data integrity.
Batch C has a documented per-table decision and owner-path evidence, even if the decision is to defer FORCE.
Batch D has a selected access model and verified cross-tenant storage denial evidence.
All 14 boundary cases are executed in both directions for 112 post-change foreign-tenant command denials.
All 28 matrix same-tenant positive controls, explicit new-row checks, service-role route cases, and all 11 public surfaces meet their postconditions.
Rollback and reapply are rehearsed in staging with no silent row or object loss.
Telemetry contains no secrets and no stop signal is present.
A fresh approval records target revision, staging evidence, production window, rollback owner, and go/no-go decision.
